thread.title: 'High casualties probable' after Venezuela quakes

author: 7NewsMelbourne
title: 'High casualties probable' after Venezuela quakes
text:
Shocking footage from Caracas captures locals fleeing the airport as the building begins to collapse.
There are fears thousands of people could be dead and injured after two huge earthquakes rocked Venezuela on Thursday morning AEST. The first quake registered as a 7.2 magnitude tremor and struck nearly 170km away from the capital of Caracas at 6.04pm on Wednesday local time .
The USGS clarified that the smaller quake was a “foreshock”, while the latter was the “mainshock”. No official casualty rates or damage estimates have been released.
However, the USGS initially estimated the death toll could be between 10,000 and 100,000, and that the disaster was widespread.
“We have buildings, homes and houses which have collapsed and we are taking care of things with everything we have available in terms of security, civil assistance,” Interior Minister Diosdado Cabello said. In Chacao, a municipality in Venezuela’s capital, mayor Gustavo Duque said 16 people had been injured and there had been fatalities, but did not specify the death toll.
Many people were at home when the earthquakes struck because June 24 was a national holiday commemorating the 1821 military victory that helped Venezuela gain independence from Spain. Dramatic footage posted online shows panicked travelers fleeing Simon Bolivar International Airport, just north of the capital, after the back-to-back earthquakes struck.
Wilmer Azuaje, a deputy for the state of Barinas, posted footage on Instagram showing crowds running as parts of the ceiling and walls fell, spreading debris and smoke throughout the building. Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodriguez has declared a state of emergency, shuting down multiple schools and airports.
